blockers.title: An operative terminalization rule still requires the removed pendingTerminalizerRecord and contradicts the reserved journal slot
blockers.finding: v10's principal repair says there is no external pending-terminalizer record: a paused-carrier terminalizer is accepted only when the reserved grant-journal terminal marker is durably appended, and an append failure is a retryable refusal outside FIRST. But the sibling terminalization clause remains live and says that a terminalizer arriving during capacityPause is stored as pendingTerminalizerRecord. That is not historical prose; both fields govern the same lifecycle branch. The old clause resurrects an external persisted byte-set that no longer has bytePlacement, class, owner, writer, lifecycle, or recovery semantics, and it recreates the second ordering/gating authority rejected by both v9 reviews. An implementation cannot satisfy both rules.
blockers.whyBlocker: The claimed SCC-V9-B1/B2 and CLAUDE-V9-B1 repair is false under composed live semantics. Following one branch preserves the one-journal order; following the other recreates the rejected unplaced external order. DR-124 is specifically the closed state-class/owner/writer contract, so an operative unassigned persisted record and contradictory terminalization rule bar acceptance.
blockers.minimumRepair: Remove or rewrite capacityPauseIsNotFailClosedNoAppend so every live capacity-pause terminalization clause uses only the reserved grant-journal marker, makes failed append a retryable refusal outside FIRST, and contains no operative pendingTerminalizerRecord reference. Re-run an all-path occurrence check and roster the exact edit. Historical v8/v9 provenance may retain the old name only when explicitly historical.

The reserved-slot design repairs the v9 ordering and failed-write defects only in its rewritten capacityPause field; an unchanged operative sibling still requires the removed external pendingTerminalizerRecord, so the composed contract remains contradictory and reopens the rejected second-order/unplaced-byte defect.
